newsitem.title: UK: Blair says British interest to prevail in Europe.
newsitem.headline: Blair says British interest to prevail in Europe.

text.p: British opposition Labour Party leader Tony Blair said on Monday there were "formidable obstacles" to Britain joining a European single currency in the first wave.

Blair, strong favourite to become Britian's next prime minister in elections expected to take place on May 1, said that in dealings with Europe the national interest would prevail both in the question of a single currency and the right to veto decisions by the European Union.
"I do not believe it is in Britain's national interest to join up to a single currency come what may," Blair told BBC radio in an interview.
"There are formidable obstacles to joining in the first wave. What is important is that the key test whenever this issue arises is Britain's national interest," Blair added.
Blair said Labour was united over the issue of Europe, in contrast to the ruling Conservatives who have been torn apart by internal dissent over the past five years.

Blair was speaking on the morning when Prime Minister John Major, whose Conservatives are trailing Labour by more than 20 points in opinion polls, was expected to officially announce a May 1 date for a national election.
